record.title: Maseru Bridge obstructions in September 2025 transport-market dispute
record.scope: Maseru Bridge passenger transport and pedestrian access, with a temporary wider vehicle obstruction
record.direction: Initial restriction targeted Lesotho vehicles entering South Africa; retaliatory obstruction affected bridge access.
record.movement: Hawkers and other passengers, Lesotho buses/minibuses, and pedestrians in the retaliatory phase.
record.exceptions: No formal exemptions documented; the bridge-wide vehicle blockade was removed by police.
record.imposing_authority: Manyatseng taxi operators and retaliating Lesotho transport operators
record.enforcement: Operators blocked vehicles and pedestrian access; vehicles parked across the bridge were impounded.
record.consequences: Stranded traders and interrupted journeys; no quantified loss estimate adopted.
record.relationship: Distinct from R3-AF-004 (2017) and R3-AF-005 (2019); shared location is not a duplicate episode.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no present closure is inferred.
record.official_rationale: South African operators sought a share of cross-border passenger business; Lesotho operators protested their exclusion. This is non-state market protection, not a government trade ban.
record.context: Dispute over transporting hawkers to Durban produced changing restrictions and retaliatory obstruction.
record.uncertainty: A 15 September witness traces being stranded to Sunday night, but the wider first onset is unclear. Smooth crossings on Sunday 21 September followed an 18 September arrangement; first reopening and full normalization are not established.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Changing vehicle/pedestrian scopes and police removal prevent treating 15–21 September as a continuous general closure.
